passages.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the command of God our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope, To Timothy, my true child in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this letter.
Paul is an apostle of Christ Jesus.
God is our Savior.
Christ Jesus is our hope.
God commanded Paul to be an apostle.
Paul writes to Timothy.
Timothy is Paul's true child in the faith.
Paul greets Timothy.
Paul asks for grace for Timothy.
Paul asks for mercy for Timothy.
Paul asks for peace for Timothy.
Grace, mercy, and peace come from God the Father.
Grace, mercy, and peace come from Christ Jesus our Lord.
passages.original: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ κατ’ ἐπιταγὴν Θεοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τῆς ἐλπίδος ἡμῶν Τιμοθέῳ γνησίῳ τέκνῳ ἐν πίστει Χάρις ἔλεος εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν

passages.text: As I urged you on my departure to Macedonia, you should stay on at Ephesus to instruct certain men not to teach false doctrines or devote themselves to myths and endless genealogies, which promote speculation rather than the stewardship of God’s work, which is by faith.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Christ Jesus by the command of God our Savior and Christ Jesus our hope.
Paul writes to Timothy, his true child in the faith.
Paul urged Timothy to remain in Ephesus when Paul left for Macedonia.
Paul wanted Timothy to give instructions to certain men.
These men must not teach false doctrines.
They must not devote themselves to myths.
They must not devote themselves to endless genealogies.
Myths and endless genealogies promote speculation.
Speculation does not help the stewardship of God’s work.
God’s work is carried out by faith.
passages.original: Καθὼς παρεκάλεσά σε προσμεῖναι ἐν Ἐφέσῳ πορευόμενος εἰς Μακεδονίαν ἵνα παραγγείλῃς τισὶν μὴ ἑτεροδιδασκαλεῖν μηδὲ προσέχειν μύθοις καὶ γενεαλογίαις ἀπεράντοις αἵτινες ἐκζητήσεις παρέχουσιν μᾶλλον ἢ οἰκονομίαν Θεοῦ τὴν ἐν πίστει

passages.text: The goal of our instruction is the love that comes from a pure heart, a clear conscience, and a sincere faith.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Christ Jesus.
God commanded Paul to serve.
Paul writes to Timothy, his true child in the faith.
Paul gives Timothy instructions.
The goal of Paul's instruction is love.
This love comes from a pure heart.
This love comes from a good conscience.
This love comes from a sincere faith.
passages.original: Τὸ δὲ τέλος τῆς παραγγελίας ἐστὶν ἀγάπη ἐκ καθαρᾶς καρδίας καὶ συνειδήσεως ἀγαθῆς καὶ πίστεως ἀνυποκρίτου

passages.text: Some have strayed from these ways and turned aside to empty talk.
passages.sermon:
Some people have missed the right way.
They have turned away from it.
They now speak empty words.
Their talk has no value.
passages.original: ὧν τινες ἀστοχήσαντες ἐξετράπησαν εἰς ματαιολογίαν

passages.text: They want to be teachers of the law, but they do not understand what they are saying or that which they so confidently assert.
passages.sermon: Some people want to be teachers of the law.\r\nThey do not understand what they are saying.\r\nThey do not understand the things they speak about with confidence.
passages.original: θέλοντες εἶναι νομοδιδάσκαλοι μὴ νοοῦντες μήτε ἃ λέγουσιν μήτε περὶ τίνων διαβεβαιοῦνται

passages.text: Now we know that the law is good, if one uses it legitimately.
passages.sermon:
The law comes from God.
The law is good.
We know this truth.
The law is good only if a person uses it properly.
A person must use the law in the right way.
passages.original: Οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι καλὸς ὁ νόμος ἐάν τις αὐτῷ νομίμως χρῆται

passages.text: We realize that law is not enacted for the righteous, but for the lawless and rebellious, for the ungodly and sinful, for the unholy and profane, for killers of father or mother, for murderers, for the sexually immoral, for homosexuals, for slave traders and liars and perjurers, and for anyone else who is averse to sound teaching that agrees with the glorious gospel of the blessed God, with which I have been entrusted.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul has been entrusted with the gospel of the blessed God.
The law is not made for righteous people.
The law is made for lawless people.
The law is made for rebellious people.
The law is made for ungodly people.
The law is made for sinful people.
The law is made for unholy people.
The law is made for profane people.
The law is made for people who kill their fathers.
The law is made for people who kill their mothers.
The law is made for murderers.
The law is made for sexually immoral people.
The law is made for homosexuals.
The law is made for slave traders.
The law is made for liars.
The law is made for perjurers.
The law is made for anyone who opposes sound teaching.
Sound teaching agrees with the glorious gospel of the blessed God.
Paul has been entrusted with this gospel.
passages.original: εἰδὼς τοῦτο ὅτι δικαίῳ νόμος οὐ κεῖται ἀνόμοις δὲ καὶ ἀνυποτάκτοις ἀσεβέσι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοῖς ἀνοσίοις καὶ βεβήλοις πατρολῴαις καὶ μητρολῴαις ἀνδροφόνοις πόρνοις ἀρσενοκοίταις ἀνδραποδισταῖς ψεύσταις ἐπιόρκοις καὶ εἴ τι ἕτερον τῇ ὑγιαινούσῃ διδασκαλίᾳ ἀντίκειται κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς δόξης τοῦ μακαρίου Θεοῦ ὃ ἐπιστεύθην ἐγώ

passages.text: I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who has strengthened me, that He considered me faithful and appointed me to service.
passages.sermon:
Christ Jesus is our Lord.
He has strengthened me.
He considered me faithful.
He appointed me to service.
I thank Christ Jesus our Lord.
passages.original: Χάριν ἔχω τῷ ἐνδυναμώσαντί με Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν ὅτι πιστόν με ἡγήσατο θέμενος εἰς διακονίαν

passages.text: I was formerly a blasphemer, a persecutor, and a violent man; yet because I had acted in ignorance and unbelief, I was shown mercy.
passages.sermon:
I was once a blasphemer.
I spoke against God.
I was a persecutor.
I attacked and harmed others.
I was a violent man.
I acted with cruelty.
I did these things because I did not know the truth.
I acted in unbelief.
God showed me mercy.
God forgave me because I acted in ignorance and unbelief.
passages.original: τὸ πρότερον ὄντα βλάσφημον καὶ διώκτην καὶ ὑβριστήν ἀλλὰ ἠλεήθην ὅτι ἀγνοῶν ἐποίησα ἐν ἀπιστίᾳ

passages.text: And the grace of our Lord overflowed to me, along with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon:
The Lord Jesus Christ is our Lord.
He gave me grace.
His grace overflowed to me.
This grace came with faith.
This grace came with love.
This faith and love are found in Christ Jesus.
passages.original: ὑπερεπλεόνασεν δὲ ἡ χάρις τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν μετὰ πίστεως καὶ ἀγάπης τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: This is a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the worst.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking.
Paul was once a blasphemer, a persecutor, and a violent man.
Paul acted in ignorance and unbelief.
God showed Paul mercy.
Paul says this statement is trustworthy.
Everyone should fully accept this statement.
Christ Jesus came into the world.
Christ Jesus came to save sinners.
Paul is the worst of the sinners.
passages.original: Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος καὶ πάσης ἀποδοχῆς ἄξιος ὅτι Χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς ἦλθεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἁμαρτωλοὺς σῶσαι ὧν πρῶτός εἰμι ἐγώ

passages.text: But for this very reason I was shown mercy, so that in me, the worst of sinners, Christ Jesus might display His perfect patience as an example to those who would believe in Him for eternal life.
passages.sermon:
I am the worst of sinners.
God showed me mercy for this reason.
Christ Jesus wanted to show His perfect patience in me.
He used me as an example.
He did this for those who would believe in Him.
He did this so they would have eternal life.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ διὰ τοῦτο ἠλεήθην ἵνα ἐν ἐμοὶ πρώτῳ ἐνδείξηται Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τὴν ἅπασαν μακροθυμίαν πρὸς ὑποτύπωσιν τῶν μελλόντων πιστεύειν ἐπ’ αὐτῷ εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον

passages.text: Now to the King eternal, immortal, and invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
passages.sermon:
God is the only God.
God is King forever.
God lives forever.
God cannot die.
God cannot be seen.
Honor belongs to God.
Glory belongs to God.
God deserves honor and glory forever.
Amen.
passages.original: Τῷ δὲ Βασιλεῖ τῶν αἰώνων ἀφθάρτῳ ἀοράτῳ μόνῳ Θεῷ τιμὴ καὶ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων ἀμήν

passages.text: Timothy, my child, I entrust you with this command in keeping with the previous prophecies about you, so that by them you may fight the good fight, holding on to faith and a good conscience, which some have rejected and thereby shipwrecked their faith.
passages.sermon:
Timothy, you are my child in the faith.
I give you this command.
I do this because of the prophecies spoken about you before.
These prophecies guide you.
Use them to fight the good fight.
Hold on to faith.
Keep a good conscience.
Some people have rejected a good conscience.
They have also turned away from faith.
They have ruined their faith.
passages.original: Ταύτην τὴν παραγγελίαν παρατίθεμαί σοι τέκνον Τιμόθεε κατὰ τὰς προαγούσας ἐπὶ σὲ προφητείας ἵνα στρατεύῃ ἐν αὐταῖς τὴν καλὴν στρατείαν ἔχων πίστιν καὶ ἀγαθὴν συνείδησιν ἥν τινες ἀπωσάμενοι περὶ τὴν πίστιν ἐναυάγησαν

passages.text: Among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have handed over to Satan to be taught not to blaspheme.
passages.sermon: Hymenaeus and Alexander are among those who rejected faith and a good conscience.\r\nI have handed Hymenaeus and Alexander over to Satan.\r\nI did this so they may be taught not to blaspheme.
passages.original: ὧν ἐστιν Ὑμέναιος καὶ Ἀλέξανδρος οὓς παρέδωκα τῷ Σατανᾷ ἵνα παιδευθῶσιν μὴ βλασφημεῖν
